note: Theory that is heard, not recited: tap the three roots on the staff, hear their chords, then follow I-IV-V by ear in two orders and backings. The staff is explained once for a beginner; works for any instrument, or none.

exercise.title: I, IV and V in G, by ear
exercise.focus: G major · roots G C D · I-IV-V-I by ear
exercise.why: Three chords carry thousands of songs, so hearing which one is playing is the start of learning songs by ear.

sections.text: The staff below shows G major; tap a note to hear it. In G major, {{1}} is G, {{4}} is C and {{5}} is D. Tap each one, then press the chord built on it in the chord boxes below.
Press Play below to hear I, IV, V, I, one bar each. Say the numeral out loud as each chord arrives.
The same three chords in a new order, with a softer backing. Press Play below and look away from the screen. Name each chord as it arrives, then look back to check.
